original_question: Are there infinitely many simple closed geodesics in every hyperbolic complete three-manifold of finite volume?
target_in_paper: Section 5.6, Question 5.6.1 (Miller, Reid): "Are there infinitely many simple closed geodesics in every hyperbolic three-manifold of finite volume?"
correct_elements: Your draft already matches the paper's target extremely closely: it asks about infinitely many simple closed geodesics, in every hyperbolic 3-manifold, under the finite-volume hypothesis. That is exactly the scope of Question 5.6.1 in Section 5.6.
missing_details: The paper's printed wording is "hyperbolic three-manifold of finite volume"; it does not explicitly insert the word "complete," although completeness is standardly implicit in this hyperbolic-manifold context.
To make the question fully stand-alone, "simple closed geodesic" should be unpacked as an embedded closed geodesic, i.e. one with no self-intersections.
The quantifier is over all finite-volume hyperbolic 3-manifolds; the paper does not add extra restrictions such as orientability, arithmeticity, cuspedness, or genericity.

The nearby discussion explicitly treats surfaces and generic negatively curved metrics only as comparison cases, so the question should not be broadened to variable negative curvature or to higher dimensions.
refined_question: Does every finite-volume hyperbolic 3-manifold contain infinitely many simple closed geodesics, i.e. infinitely many embedded closed geodesics?
justification: The draft is essentially a near-verbatim restatement of Question 5.6.1 in the survey. The only real adjustment needed is to restore the paper's exact scope and wording: the official question is about finite-volume hyperbolic 3-manifolds, with no added hypotheses, and the neighboring sentences show that broader variants for variable negative curvature or other dimensions are separate questions, not part of the main target. Adding a parenthetical definition of "simple" makes the rewritten question self-contained while staying faithful to the paper.
